invariants: Actual Windows root and one recorded descendant are alive at the ready barrier and both exit after explicit terminate, running AbortSignal, Cordis fiber disposal and direct Host exit.
Direct Host exit retains code 23; the other selected journeys exit 0 with empty stdout/stderr.
Opened process handles preserve exact physical ownership throughout observation and fallback cleanup; success is determined before any observer cleanup.
Python 3.8 thread-executor exit hook is registered before subprocess runtime finalization, so runtime cleanup precedes blocking worker joins at interpreter exit.
Actual extracted embedded Python 3.8.10 executes the same four physical journeys with exact declared product-module provenance.
identity: Exact live Windows process handles for the published root and descendant; raw pids and cwd retained separately from namespace-independent comparisons.
ownership: The Cordis runtime owns the live tree until normal disposal or observable Host finalization; the observer may clean only the two recorded live handles after failed observations.
ordering: Publish readiness, open live process handles, issue selected shutdown trigger, join Host and tree, record outcome before failure cleanup.
errors: Readiness, malformed identities, wrong Host exit, surviving children, foreign modules and diagnostics fail the gate; no blanket cleanup masks failures.
cancellation: A running source/native AbortSignal terminates the actual tree. Hard-killed Hosts, root-already-exited or unknown descendants are not this contract.
adaptation: Pinned TypeScript standard-decorator loading is a development observer only. Native imports the Python 3.8 thread-executor module before registering its reversible atexit hook.
open_questions: Clean shared candidate and actual extracted acceptance remain pending. Terminal/WinPTY, physical unhandled-rejection/crash source paths, unknown orphans, POSIX trees, Jobs and deferred Win7 remain unaccepted.
